la:verb:adorior.html:
ăd-ŏrĭor, ortus, 4, v. dep. (
part. adorsus, ; see the passage at the end of this art.; the second and third pers. of the pres. ind., acc. to the fourth conj.: adorīris, adorītur; forms analogous to orĕris, orĭtur, of the simple verb occur in ; Lucil. ap. P.), to rise up for the purpose of going to some one or something, or of undertaking something great, difficult, or hazardous (clandestinely, artfully, when a hostile approach is spoken of; while aggredi indicates a direct, open attack from a distance: aggredimur de longinquo; adorimur ex insidiis et ex proximo; nam adoriri est quasi ad aliquem oriri, i. e. exsurgere, Don. ad ; cf. the same ad Heaut. 4, 5, 9).
In gen., to approach a person in order to address him, to ask something of him, to accost, etc. (cf. accedo, adeo): cesso hunc adoriri? (quasi de improviso alloqui, Don.),: si ab eo nil fiet, tum hunc adorior hospitem,.—
Esp.
To approach one with hostile intent, to assault, assail, Lucil. ap. P.: inermem tribunum gladiis,: a tergo Milonem,: navem,: impeditos adoriebantur,: hos Conon adortus magno proelio fugat,: urbem vi,: oppugnatio eos aliquanto atrocior quam ante adorta est,; cf. 21, 28: praetorem ex improviso in itinere adortus,: variis criminationibus,: minis,: jurgio,: senatum,.—Also absol., .—
To enter upon any course of action, esp. to engage in or undertake any thing difficult or dangerous; with acc. or inf.: commutare animum quicumque adoritur,: ne convellere adoriamur ea, quae non possint commoveri,; : Ἡρακλείδιον, si Brundisium salvi, adoriemur (sc. scribere), ; : majus adorta nefas,: hi dominam Ditis thalamo deducere adorti,; cf. ; .—So esp. in the histt., : hanc (Munychiam) bis tyranni oppugnare sunt adorti,; so also ; ; ; 40, 22; 43, 21; 44, 12; cf. also 3, 44: hanc virginem Appius pretio ac spe pellicere adortus.— Once in the form of the part. perf. adorsus: qui Hippiam tyrannum interficere adorsi erant,.

la:verb:adoro.gloss: to speak to, accost, address; negotiate a matter with
senses: to speak to, accost, address; negotiate a matter with
to speak to someone to obtain something; ask, entreat, pray to, beseech, implore, plead
to admire, esteem highly, marvel at, revere
la:verb:adoro.html:
ăd-ōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
In the earliest per., to speak to or accost one, to address; hence, also, to treat of or negotiate a matter with one: adorare veteribus est alloqui,: immo cum gemitu populum sic adorat,; , p. 130: adorare apud antiquos significabat agere: unde et legati oratores dicuntur, quia mandata populi agunt, Paul. ex Müll.; cf. oro and orator.— Hence, also, in judicial lang., to bring an accusation, to accuse; so in the Fragm. of the XII. Tab. lex viii.: SEI (Si) ADORAT FVRTO QVOD NEC MANIFESTVM ERIT, Fest. S. V. NEC, p. 162 Müll.—
In the class. per., to speak to one in order to obtain something of him; to ask or entreat one, esp. a deity, to pray earnestly, to beseech, supplicate, implore; constr. with acc., ut, or the simple subj.: quos adorent, ad quos precentur et supplicent,: affaturque deos et sanctum sidus adorat,: in rupes, in saxa (volens vos Turnus adoro) Ferte ratem,: Junonis prece numen,: prece superos,: non te per meritum adoro,.—With the thing asked for in the acc. (like rogo, peto, postulo): cum hostiā caesā pacem deūm adorāsset, Drak.—With ut: adoravi deos, ut, etc.,; : adorati di, ut bene ac feliciter eveniret,: Hanc ego, non ut me defendere temptet, adoro,.—With the subj. without ut, poet.: maneat sic semper adoro,I pray,.—
Hence,
Dropping the idea of asking, entreating, to reverence, honor, adore, worship the gods or objects of nature regarded as gods; more emphatic than venerari, and denoting the highest degree of reverence (Gr. προσκυνεῖν); the habitus adorantium was to put the right hand to the mouth and turn about the entire body to the right (dextratio, q. v.); cf. ; ; . —Constr. with acc., dat., with prepp. or absol.
With acc.: Auctoremque viae Phoebum taciturnus adorat,: Janus adorandus,: in delubra non nisi adoraturus intras,: large deos adorare,: nil praeter nubes et caeli numen adorat,: adorare crocodilon,.— In eccl. Lat. of the worship of the true God: adoravit Israel Deum,: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis,: Deum adora,; so of Christ: videntes eum adoraverunt,; adorent eum omnes angeli Dei,.—
With dat. (eccl.): adorato (imperat.) Domino Deo tuo, : nec adorabis deo alieno, Mai (deum alienum, Vulg.): qui adorant sculptibus, Mai (sculptilia, Vulg.).—
With prepp. (eccl.): si adoraveris coram me,: adorabunt in conspectu tuo,: adorent ante pedes tuos,; .—
Absol. (eccl.): Patres nostri in hoc monte adoraverunt,bis.; .—And,
The notion of religious regard being dropped, to reverence, admire, esteem highly: adorare priscorum in inveniendo curam,: Ennium sicut sacros vetustate lucos adoremus,: veteris qui tollunt grandia templi pocula adorandae rubiginis,: nec tu divinam Aeneida tenta, Sed longe sequere et vestigia semper adora,.—
Under the emperors the Oriental custom being introduced of worshipping the Cæsars with divine ceremony, to worship, to reverence: C. Caesarem adorari ut deum constituit, cum reversus ex Syria, non aliter adire ausus esset quam capite velato circumvertensque se, deinde procumbens,; ; : non salutari, sed adorari se jubet (Alexander),: adorare Caesarum imagines,: coronam a judicibus ad se delatam adoravit, did obeisancebefore, : adorare purpuram principis,i. e. touched his purple robe and brought it to the mouth in reverence,.—Of adulation to the rabble, to pay court to: nec deerat Otho protendens manus, adorare volgum,.!*? This word does not occur in Cic.; for in Arch. 11, 28, where adoravi was given by Mai in Fragm. p. 124, Halm reads adhortatus sum, and B. and K. adornavi.

la:verb:adoleo.gloss: to magnify or pile up with for sacrifice; burn, sacrifice
senses: to magnify or pile up with for sacrifice; burn, sacrifice
to consume or destroy by fire, burn
la:verb:adoleo.html:
ăd-ŏlĕo, ui. ultum, 2, v. a.
oleo
.
To magnify; hence, in sacrificial language, to which this word chiefly belongs, to honor, to worship, or to offer in worship, to sacrifice, burn, according as it has such words as deos, aras, etc., or hostiam, viscera, and tura, for its object; v. explanation of this word in : Adolere verbum est proprie sacra reddentium, quod significat votis ac supplicationibus numen auctius facere; and Adolere est urere, Verg. in Bucol. [8, 65],verbenasque adole pinguis et mascula tura. Adolere, augere, honorare, propitiare; et est verbum sacratum, ut macte, magis aucte. etc.; so : Flammis adolere penates, i. e. colere, sed adolere est proprie augere. In sacris autem, κατʼ εὐφημισμόν, adolere per bonum omen dicitur, nam in aris non adolentur aliqua, sed cremantur,) and ad E. 8, 65: Adole: incende, sed κατʼ εὐφημισμὸν dicitur; nam adole est auge (not used in Cic.): sanguine conspergunt aras adolentque altaria donis,cover the altar with gifts,: castis adolet dum altaria taedis,: verbenasque adole pingues et mascula tura, (on which Serv. l. l.): flammis adolere penates, : viscera tauri,; : focos,: cruore captivo adolere aras,to sprinkle the altars with the blood of captives,: precibus et igne puro altaria adolentur,: adolere honores, to honor the gods by offered gifts: Junoni Argivae jussos adolemus honores,: nullos aris adoleret honores,.—
In later Lat., in gen., to burn, consume by fire: ut leves stipulae demptis adolentur aristis,: id (corpus) igne adoleatur,: ut Aeneida, quam nondum satis elimāsset, adolerent,: quas (prunas) gravi frigore adoleri multas jusserat,.

la:verb:adoperio.html:
ăd-ŏpĕrĭo, ĕrŭi, ertum, 4, v. a.,
to cover up or over (not used before the Aug. per., and gen. in the part. perf. pass.): capite adoperto,; , and : purpureo adopertus amictu,: tempora adoperta cucullo,: adopertam floribus humum,; cf. : hiems gelu,: aether nubibus,: lumina somno,: tenebris mors,: foribus adopertis,with closed doors,.—In the verb. finit.: Quidam prius tuto sale sex horis (ova) adoperiunt,: pellem setis adoperuit, Lact. Op. Dei, 7.—Hence, ădŏpertē, adv., v.the foll. art.

la:noun:ador.gloss: a kind of hulled wheat of the genus Triticum: emmer, farro, or spelt
senses: a kind of hulled wheat of the genus Triticum: emmer, farro, or spelt
la:noun:ador.html:
ădor, ŏris and ōris, n.
cf. 1. edo, ἔδομαι, Engl. to eat, Goth. ita, Sanscr. admi; and Ang.-Sax. ata = Engl. oat, and Sanscr. annam (for adnam) = food, corn
,
a kind of grain, spelt, Triticum spelta, Linn. (acc. to Paul. ex Fest.: Ador farris genus, edor quondam appellatum ab edendo, vel quod aduratur, ut fiat tostum, unde in sacrificio mola salsa officitur, p. 3 Müll.: Ador frumenti genus, quod epulis et immolationibus sacris pium putatur, unde et adorare, propitiare religiones, potest dictum videri,): cum pater ipse domus palea porrectus in horna Esset ador loliumque,: adŏris de polline, Aus. Mon. de Cibis, p. 238; Gannius ap. : satos adŏris stravisse,: ardor adōris, (Ador is often indeclinable, acc. to P.)

la:verb:adolesco.gloss: to grow up, become an adult, mature
senses: to grow up, become an adult, mature
to grow, increase, augment, become greater
la:verb:adolesco.html:
ăd-ŏlesco, ēvi (rare
ui, Varr. ap. P.; adolēsse sync. for adolevisse,), ultum, 3, v. inch. [1. adoleo], to grow up, to grow (of everything capable of increase in magnitude).
In gen.
Lit., of men, animals, plants; seasons, passions, etc.; but esp. of age: postquam adolevit ad eam aetatem, uti, etc.,: ubi robustis adolevit viribus aetas,; cf. 4, 1035; 2, 1123: adultum robur,; : postquam adoluerit haec juventus, Varr. ap. P.: qui adoleverit,: viriditas herbescens, quae sensim adolescit,: ter senos proles adoleverat annos,: adolescere ramos cernat,: adolēsse segetes,: simul atque adoleverit aetas,: cum matura adoleverit aetas,.—Hence, transf. from age to the person, to grow up, come to maturity, mature: adulta virgo,: arundines non sine imbre adolescunt,: in amplitudinem,: in crassitudinem,; so 16, 34, 62, § 151; 8, 14, 14, § 36 al.: ac dum prima novis adolescit frondibus aetas,: quoad capillus adolesceret,. —
Fig., to grow, increase, augment, to become greater: cupiditas agendi adolescit una cum aetatibus,: ratio cum adolevit,: ingenium brevi adolevit,: postquam res publica adolevit,; : quantum superbiae socordiaeque Vitellio adoleverit,: Cremona numero colonorum, adolevit,: ver adolescit,advances,; : caepe revirescit, decedente luna, inarescit adolescente,.—
Esp., in sacrificial lang., to be kindled, to burn (cf. 1. adoleo): Panchaeis adolescunt ignibus arae,.—Hence, ădŏlescens, entis, v. adules-.—ădultus, a, um, P. a., grown up, adult.
Lit.
Of living beings: Ab his ipsis (virginibus), cum jam essent adultae,; so, virgo,; ; ; cf.: adultae aetate virgines,: pueri,: liberi,: filius,: catuli,: locustae,: fetus (apum),.—Comp.: (hirundinum) pullorum adultiores,.—
Of things (concrete and abstract): vitium propagine,: crinis,: lanugo,: aetas,; : aestas,advanced,: autumnus,. 31: nox,.—
Fig., grown, matured, adult: populus adultus jam paene et pubes,; so, qui non nascentibus Athenis, sed jam adultis fuerunt,; cf.: nascenti adhuc (eloquentiae) nec satis adultae,: res nondum adultae,: pestis rei publicae (of Catiline),: auctoritas nondum adulta,: conjuratio,; cf.: incipiens adhuc et necdum adulta seditio,

la:adj:adoreus.html:
ădōrĕus, a, um, adj.
ador
,
pertaining to spelt, consisting of spelt.
Adj.: far adoreum = ador,; ; : semen,; : liba,: bellaria,.—
Subst.
ădōrĕa (adoria, Paul. ex Müll.; see below), ae, f. (sc. donatio), a reward of valor (in early ages this usually consisted of grain); hence, trop., glory, fame, renown: gloriam denique ipsam a farris honore adoream appellabant,; : praedā agroque adoreāque affecit populares suos,: pulcher fugatis Ille dies Latio tenebris, Qui primus almā risit adoreā, in lordly honor, viz. by the defeat of Hasdrubal, . (Festus gives another explanation for the signif. honor, renown, etc.: adoriam laudem sive gloriam dicebant, quia gloriosum eum putabant esse, qui farris copia abundaret, Müll.). —
ădōrĕum. i, n. (sc. far), i. q. ador, spelt, .

la:noun:adorea.html: ădōrĕa, ae, and ădōrĕum, i, see the foll. art., II. A. and B.

la:adj:adoptivus.html:
ădoptīvus, a, um, adj.
adopto
,
pertaining to adoption, made or acquired by adoption, adoptive: filius, an adopted son: P. Scipio, Fragm. ap. (opp. naturalis, a son by birth): filiorum neque naturalem Drusum neque adoptivum Germanicum patria caritate dilexit,: pater adoptivus, who has adopted one as son (or grandson, v. adoptio), an adoptive father, : frater, soror, etc., a brother, sister, etc., by adoption, not by birth, , and 38, 8, 3; so also, familia,the family into which one has been received by adoption,: adoptiva sacra, of the family into which one has been adopled (opp. paterna): neque amissis sacris paternis in haec adoptiva venisti,: nomen, received by adoption (opp. nomen gentile), : nobilitas,nobility acquired by adoption,.—Transf., of the ingrafting of plants (cf. adoptio): fissaque adoptivas accipit arbor opes,bears fruits not natural to it, ingrafted,; : quae sit adoptivis arbor onusta comis,; cf. 144, 160 (cf. : Miraturque (arbos) novas frondes et non sua poma).

la:noun:adoptio.html:
ădoptĭo, ōnis, f.
v. adoptatio
,
a taking or receiving of one in the place of a child (also of a grandchild, ), an adopting, adoption (properly of one still under paternal authority, in patria potestate; on the contr., arrogatio referred to one who was already independent, homo sui juris. The former took place before the praetor or other magistrate and five witnesses, by a threefold mancipatio, i. e. sham sale; the latter could only be effected before the assembled people in the comitia curiata,; ; . More used than adoptatio, q. v.): emancipare filium alicui in adoptionem,: dare se alicui in adoptionem,; ; cf. : adscire aliquem per adoptionem,; or, in adoptionem,: inserere aliquem familiae per adoptionem,: adscitus adoptione in imperium et cognomentum,: adoptio in Domitium festinatur,: adoptionem nuncupare,to make known, to announce,: adoptio consularis, performed by a consul, Quint. prooem. 6, 13 Spald. al.—
Transf., of plants, the ingrafting, Plin. prooem. 1, 16.—Of bees, the admittance to or reception in a new hive: ut tamquam novae prolis adoptione domicilia confirmentur,.—In eccl. Lat., in spiritual sense of adoption as children of God: adoptionem filiorum Dei,; ; .

la:verb:adopto.gloss: to take by choice, choose, select
senses: to take by choice, choose, select
to take someone into a family, adopt
la:verb:adopto.html:
ăd-opto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to take to one's self by wish, choice (optando); to choose, select.
In gen.: sociam te mihi adopto ad meam salutem,: qui manstutorem me adoptavit bonis,who has chosen me as a guardian of his property,: quem sibi illa (provincia) defensorem sui juris adoptavit,: eum sibi patronum, id : quem potius adoptem aut invocem, Vatin. ap. : Frater, Pater, adde; Ut cuique est aetas, ita quemque facetus adopta (i. e. adscisce, adjunge, sc. tuo alloquio, Cruqu.), make him by thy greeting a father, brother, etc., i. e. call him, : Etruscas Turnus adoptat opes,strives after,.—Hence: adoptare se alicui, to give or attach one's self to: qui se potentiae causā Caesaris libertis adoptāsset,.—
Esp. as t. t., to take one in the place of a child or grandchild, to adopt (diff. from arrogo; v. adoptio).
Lit., constr. with aliquem, also with ab aliquo aliquem (from the real father, a patre naturali), (cf. ): adoptat illum puerum subreptitium sibi filium,: filium senatorem populum Romanum sibi velle adoptare,: adoptatus patricius a plebeio,: is qui hunc minorem Scipionem a Paulo adoptavit,: adoptavit eum heredemque fecit ex dodrante,: adoptatus testamento,: adoptari a se Pisonem pronuntiat, : Pisonem pro contione adoptavit,: quem illa adoptavit,.—With in and acc.: in regnum,: in familiam nomenque,: in successionem,.—
Fig.: servi in bona libertatis nostrae adoptantur,are, as it were, adopted into freedom, are made participants of freedom,; and of ingrafting (cf. adoptivus): venerit insitio: fac ramum ramus adoptet,; so . Those who were adopted commonly received the family name of the adoptive father, with the ending -anus, e. g. Aemilianus, Pomponianus, etc.—Hence Cic. says ironic. of one who appropriated to himself the name of another: ipse se adoptat: et C. Stalenus, qui se ipse adoptaverat et de Staleno Aelium fecerat,had changed himself from a Stalenus to an Ælius,; and Vitruv.: Zoilus qui adoptavit cognomen, ut Homeromastix vocitaretur, had himself called, 7, 8. So: ergo aliquod gratum Musis tibi nomen adopta,; in Pliny, very often, adoptare aliquid (also with the addition of nomine suo or in nomen), to give a thing its name: Baetis Oceanum Atlanticum, provinciam adoptans, petit, while it gives to the province the name (Baetica). : A Zmyrna Hermus campos facit et nomini suo adoptat,; so 25, 3, 7, § 22: in nomen,; so also Statius, Theb. 7, 259.

la:verb:adorno.gloss: to get ready, furnish, equip, provide, fit out
senses: to get ready, furnish, equip, provide, fit out
la:verb:adorno.html:
ăd-orno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to prepare a thing for some definite object, to get ready, to furnish, provide, fit out, equip, κοσμέω.
In gen. (class.; esp. freq. in Plaut. and Cic.): quin tu mihi adornas ad fugam viaticum,: nuptias,; so also : fugam, (cf.: fugam aut furtum parat,): maria classibus et praesidiis,: forum comitiumque adornatum, ad speciem magnifico ornatu, ad sensum cogitationemque acerbo et lugubri,: ut accusationem et petitionem consulatus adornet atque instruat,prepare,: testium copiam,to produce,: invenire et adornare comparationem criminis,: contra haec Pompeius naves magnas onerarias adornabat,: omni opulentiā insignium armorum bellum adornaverant,.—Anteclass. constr. with inf.: tragulam in te inicere adornat,.—And absol.: adorna, ut rem divinam faciam,; .—
To put an ornament upon one; hence, to decorate, adorn, embellish with something (mostly in the Aug. per.; esp. in the histt.): aliquem aliqua re: (Numa) flaminem insigni veste et curuli regiā sellā adornavit,: triumphum,; so ; ; ; ; :

; —Trop.: tantis adornatus virtutibus,: praecipuis donis,: bene facta suis verbis,: adornata verbis,: legem leviter (sc. verbis) adornabit, ut justam,.—Hence, * ădornātē, adv.: declamabat splendide atque adornate, brilliantly and elegantly (opp. circumcise ac sordide), .

la:noun:adonidium.gloss: alternative form of adōnium (“type of meter”)
senses: alternative form of adōnium (“type of meter”)

la:noun:adoptatio.html:
ădoptātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.; access. form of adoptio, by which it was supplanted after the class. per.
,
an adopting, receiving as a child, υἱοθεσία: quid propagatio nominis, quid adoptationes filiorum,: adoptatio Theophani agitata est,: ipsum illum adoptatione in regnum pervenisse,: quod per praetorem fit, adoptatio dicitur; quod per populum, arrogatio,; .
